content_sections.heading: About MoEF&CC
content_sections.text: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change is a Government of India ministry. Its Hazardous Substances Management (HSM) Division, which is making this engagement, works from Indira Paryavaran Bhawan on Jor Bagh Road in New Delhi.

content_sections.heading: MoEF&CC Scientific Consultant Vacancy Details 2026
content_sections.text: The consolidated amount includes all applicable taxes, and no other facility or allowance is allowed. Consultants are not entitled to Dearness Allowance, Residential Telephone, Residential Accommodation, Personal Staff, CGHS or Medical Reimbursement. The annual increment is between 0 and 8 percent, depending on the quality of performance as determined by the Divisional Head case by case. FREEJOBALERT DAILY QUIZ Preparing for Govt Exams? content_sections.heading: MoEF&CC Scientific Consultant Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Master's Degree in Env. Engineering/ Environmental Science/Chemistry or B.E/B.Tech. Both posts also require good knowledge and experience of M.S. Office. Experience includes up to 3 years for Ph.D holders, provided no experience is counted during those 3 years. Persons with M.Phil, M.Tech., M.Sc., Ph.D. Excellent communication and writing skills Experience shall be in the relevant field of specialized work, with good computer skills. You should be well versed with the subject and the current policy framework of the central and state governments. You should be familiar with international conventions and treaties related to the subject. You must have proven ability to coordinate and deliver multidisciplinary, multi-institutional programs and projects related to the subject. You must have the analytical ability to process the information available. You must have scientific publications in the relevant areas in recognized peer reviewed scientific journals. See the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of each post.

rows.work_experience: More than 5 years and upto 10 years in reputed institutions in the relevant field
More than 10 years and upto 16 years in reputed institutions in the relevant field

content_sections.heading: Duties of the Scientific Consultants
content_sections.text: Work related to the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, as amended from time to time Assisting the Ministry in monitoring and implementing solid and liquid waste management rules and Extended Producer Responsibility on Glass, Paper and Sanitary wastes Organizing Task Force and Central Monitoring Committee meetings, and preparing their agenda and minutes Preparing brief notes on the rules and EPR guidelines, and concept notes or agenda for related events Collecting and collating grievances related to the online portal Analyzing media reports and articles, and gathering reports on international best practices for solid and liquid waste Assisting in drafting amendments on Solid waste, Liquid waste and EPR Organizing conferences, meetings and seminars, developing a related database, and other assigned tasks Assisting in implementing Circular economy action plans Reviewing and analysing circular economy aspects such as recycling of wastes Assisting in draft policies, rules and guidelines on Extended Producer Responsibility, labelling, recycling efficiency and recovery for various waste streams Assisting in international activities on resource efficiency, circular economy, sustainable consumption and production/SDG 12, and in events such as the World Circular Economy Forum Coordinating with stakeholder Ministries, departments and organisations in the Union and State Governments Developing a circular economy database, including data on EPR frameworks for different waste streams Drafting inputs on decisions and declarations of multilateral bodies such as G20, BRICS and UNEA Any other work assigned from time to time

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is by interview. Applications received in the Ministry will be scrutinized, and only shortlisted candidates shall be called. The Ministry reserves the right to call any number of applicants based on their essential and desirable qualification and experience, and preference will be given to those with adequate qualifications and experience. A request for a virtual interview shall not be considered.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: Place of work: MoEFCC, HQ at New Delhi. Tenure: Upto three years (1+1+1), subject to performance and the professional's presence being highly useful to the Division. Continuation for upto two more years will be considered case by case with the approval of the Competent Authority. Nature of appointment: Temporary (non-official), purely contractual and full time, with no other assignment permitted during the consultancy. No request for promotion shall be entertained. Termination: The Ministry can cancel the appointment at any time without assigning any reason. Absence for a continuous period of 8 days without information or valid reason leads to automatic termination. Reporting: Consultants report to the Director/Dy. Secretary under the overall supervision of the Joint Secretary or equivalent. Working hours: Same as regular Government employees in the Ministry, with attendance marked in the Biometric system. Monthly remuneration may be deducted for coming late. No extra remuneration is allowed for working beyond office hours or on holidays, and compensatory leave is at the Divisional Head's discretion. Leave: Paid leave accrues at 1.5 days for each completed month of service. No remuneration is drawn for absence beyond 18 days in a year (pro-rata). Unused leave cannot be carried forward to the next 1-year tenure. Female consultants are eligible for maternity leave under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 and the Maternity Leave Rules based on it. Official travel: TA, DA and hotel accommodation for official work are allowed under SR 190 and MoEFCC guidelines Admin-43012/1/2022 – P-II [E-176223] dated 15 April 2025. No TA/DA is admissible for joining the assignment or on its completion. Confidentiality: Consultants are subject to the Indian Official Secret Act, 1923. Internal reports and data cannot be used for research papers or books, and publishing or broadcasting information gathered on the assignment needs the Ministry's previous sanction. Conduct: Engagement is liable to be discontinued without any reason being assigned if services are found unsatisfactory or in conflict with Government interests.

faq.question: Q1. Do I need to apply by both post and email?
faq.answer: Yes. The notice asks for the signed hard copy by post and also the application by email, and both should reach by the due date.

faq.question: Q2. How is the last date of 20 November 2026 worked out?
faq.answer: The notice allows 21 days from publication of the advertisement on the Ministry's website and itself fixes that as 20 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What should I write on the envelope?
faq.answer: Clearly superscribe the name of the post you are applying for, such as Scientific Consultant Grade-I (Solid Waste Management).

faq.question: Q4. Are scientific publications compulsory?
faq.answer: Yes. Applicants for both posts must have publications in the relevant areas in recognized peer reviewed scientific journals. The form also has a section for publication details.

faq.question: Q5. Does a Ph.D count towards experience?
faq.answer: Up to 3 years of experience is included for Ph.D holders, provided no experience is counted during those 3 years.

faq.question: Q6. Will the Ministry pay for travel to the interview?
faq.answer: No. No TA/DA will be provided for appearing in the interview, and it cannot be attended virtually.

faq.question: Q7. How long can a consultant stay in this engagement?
faq.answer: The initial engagement is upto three years, renewed in 1+1+1 steps. With approval, it may run for upto two additional years, making five years in all.

faq.question: Q8. What must selected candidates submit?
faq.answer: Selected candidates shall provide an integrity certificate from 2 references known to them. They must also give a self-undertaking that they have no criminal record and no criminal case pending in any court.

faq.question: Q9. What details does the application form ask for?
faq.answer: Annexure-I has 16 items, including domicile, nationality, essential and desirable qualifications, essential and desirable work experience, training programmes attended, publications and languages known.
